journeyEntries.title: Week 12: Care plan engine v2 shipped
journeyEntries.excerpt: After three months of rebuilds and customer interviews, we shipped a new care-path recommendation engine that cut clinical onboarding time by 18%.
journeyEntries.body:
This was one of the largest internal shifts we've had as a team. We rebuilt the recommendation engine end-to-end, redesigned the data ingestion layer, and introduced a new feedback loop between clinicians and patients. Early signals show better adherence and a measurable drop in the time it takes to activate a new care plan.

This is the kind of foundational work that doesn't always look glamorous from the outside but compounds heavily over time. Every part of the product gets faster, more reliable, and more accurate when this layer improves.

journeyEntries.title: Founder note: what we learned from 42 user interviews
journeyEntries.excerpt: Most users didn't want more features. They wanted fewer, better integrated ones. So we simplified onboarding into a single guided experience.
journeyEntries.body:
Across 42 conversations, the same theme came back again and again: users were tired of fragmented tools. They didn't want a new dashboard, a new portal, or a new app. They wanted one consistent place to do their most important daily work.

That insight reshaped our roadmap. We pulled three planned features out of the next release and replaced them with a single guided onboarding flow. Six weeks later, activation rates have nearly doubled and time-to-first-value has dropped from 11 minutes to under 4.

journeyEntries.title: Product milestone: first 1,000 recurring check-ins
journeyEntries.excerpt: Crossing 1,000 recurring weekly check-ins is more than a vanity metric — it tells us the loop works.
journeyEntries.body:
We hit 1,000 recurring weekly check-ins this week. What matters isn't the round number — it's that retention curves have flattened, weekly active usage is climbing, and clinician summaries are being read on average 2.4 times each.

The product is now sticky enough that compounding effects are showing up in the data. Going from here, our focus is on making each weekly summary more actionable and on shortening the gap between insight and intervention.

journeyEntries.title: Behind the scenes: rebuilding our underwriting pipeline
journeyEntries.excerpt: Why we tore down the underwriting pipeline rather than patch it — and what we learned from the rebuild.
journeyEntries.body:
Our underwriting pipeline was the bottleneck slowing every other part of the platform. Patching it kept buying us a few more weeks; tearing it down forced us to confront the actual structural problem: too many handoffs, too many manual steps, too little observability.

The rebuild took six weeks. Today, we run underwriting in 38% of the original time, with significantly better error tracing. More importantly, the team can now ship improvements without fearing what breaks downstream.

journeyEntries.title: Hiring the right people slowly beats hiring the wrong people quickly
journeyEntries.excerpt: We're 9 people. Each hire took longer than expected — and that turned out to be a feature, not a bug.
journeyEntries.body:
Every founder gets the advice to hire fast. We didn't. Each new hire took us between 6 and 11 weeks to close. In the moment it felt painful — we were always one engineer short of where we wanted to be. In hindsight, it was the right pace.

A team this size cannot afford a wrong hire. The cost is not just the salary; it's the cultural drag, the rework, and the trust erosion. Slower hiring forced us to be sharper about what we actually needed and to invest in onboarding so that every hire ramps fast.

journeyEntries.title: How we run our weekly investor update
journeyEntries.excerpt: A simple template, a 30-minute weekly ritual, and full transparency. Here's the format we use.
journeyEntries.body:
Every Friday morning we send the same investor update: top metrics, what shipped, what didn't, what we're worried about, and what we need help with. Five sections. No spin. The goal isn't to look good — it's to keep our backers as close to the truth of the business as we are.

The format takes ~30 minutes to write because the discipline is in the data, not the language. If we don't have answers, we say so. If something broke, we name it. The compounding effect of doing this for a year is significant — investors trust the team and the data, and conversations move faster every time.

journeyEntries.title: Q3 retrospective: what worked, what didn't
journeyEntries.excerpt: An honest look at the past quarter — three things we got right and two we got wrong.
journeyEntries.body:
We started the quarter with three priorities: ship the new pricing tier, close two enterprise pilots, and reduce monthly churn. We hit the first two and missed the third — churn ended at 2.7% versus our 2.2% target.

What worked: a small, dedicated pricing pod that owned the launch end-to-end; tight scoping on enterprise contracts that kept legal cycles short. What didn't: we under-invested in proactive customer health monitoring. We're correcting that now, and a dedicated CS hire is already in flight.

journeyEntries.title: Why we're building this category, not joining it
journeyEntries.excerpt: The market is crowded with tools. We think the category itself is mis-shaped. Here's our thesis.
journeyEntries.body:
If you survey the existing tools in this space, you'll find dozens. They're well-funded, well-marketed, and superficially impressive. But every customer we've spoken with — without exception — describes the category as 'broken in the middle.'

The tools work for the edges (initial onboarding, end-of-quarter reporting) but break in the daily work in the middle. That's the gap we're building into. Not a better dashboard. Not a better integration. A re-shaping of the everyday workflow that the existing category quietly ignores.

How dependent is the model on continued macro tailwinds in this category?

qaReplies: We allocate by milestone ROI: product reliability first, then market expansion where retention is strongest. Capital follows proof of usage, not projections.
Monitor weekly activated units and conversion from pilot to recurring portfolio contracts. Those two are the cleanest leading indicators.
Cohort churn has been steady around 2.4% monthly. Our base case for next quarter is 2.6% with the new tier rollout.
Defensibility comes from data depth, not surface features. Every active customer compounds the model's underwriting accuracy.
At current velocity, $1M ARR is realistic by Q3. We've intentionally slowed sales to fix retention drivers first.
Unit economics improve as we shift toward inbound. CAC has dropped 31% over the last six months as content compounds.
Top channel CAC payback is 7 months, second channel 11 months, and the third channel is being tested before scaling.
Next hire is a senior product engineer focused on the analytics layer — that unlocks our enterprise reporting roadmap.
The model is structurally resilient even in flat markets — most of our value comes from operational efficiency, not asset appreciation.
Largest active risk is integration complexity with legacy partners. We've now built a dedicated team around it and shipped two adapters.
